newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRISH JULY CONSUMER PRICES FELL 0.1 PCT M/M - CSO.
newsitem.headline: IRISH JULY CONSUMER PRICES FELL 0.1 PCT M/M - CSO.

text.p: Irish July consumer prices, as measured by the consumer price index, fell 0.1 percent on the month, Central Statistics Office (CSO) data showed on Thursday.
Economists had forecast a rise of 0.2 to 0.3 percent while a year-on-year comparison was not available due to a lack of data for July last year.
On an 11-month basis, the index rose 1.2 percent from August 1996.
The European Union harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP), which is used for intra-EU comparison, was down 0.3 percent on the month and rose 0.8 percent in the 11 months since last August.
